issues.description: The problem statement and template imply Animals (and their subclasses) should be constructed with a single String name (UML shows only attribute 'name' and Main.java uses single-argument constructors), but the solution's Animal and subclasses define constructors expecting (String name, int age) and add an extra 'age' attribute. This mismatch between expected constructor signatures will confuse students (and the provided Main example) and makes the solution structurally incompatible with the exercise specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/signatures consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute and use single-argument constructors (String name) in the solution for Animal and all subclasses to match the UML and template Main, or (B) update the problem statement and template (including the UML and Main example) to include the 'age' attribute and require (String name, int age) constructors everywhere.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for Animal subclasses: the problem statement UML and the template Main() examples imply single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), but the solution implements constructors that take (String name, int age) (introducing an additional 'age' parameter). This API mismatch (different constructor parameter lists) breaks the conceptual mapping between the exercise description/template examples and the provided solution, and will likely confuse students when they try the example Main code or follow the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor expectations consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to provide single-argument constructors (e.g., public Seal(String name)) to match the UML/template Main examples, or (B) update the problem statement UML and the template Main examples to require/illustrate two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and adjust all class constructors in the solution accordingly. Also ensure the Main example matches the chosen constructor signature.
